articles.title_orig: China has ‘normalized’ naval presence near Japan since political spat of 2025
articles.title_zh: China has ‘normalized’ naval presence near Japan since political spat of 2025
articles.content_orig:
NEW TAIPEI CITY, Taiwan — In early November, Taiwan’s National Security Council secretary-general tracked more than 100 Chinese military-linked vessels near his island.
But given its scale, the massive flotilla that included coast guard vessels alongside navy warships may have had Taiwan’s maritime neighbor Japan in its sights, military experts say.
They say China has sent an outsized number of its far-seas naval deployments to near Japan’s southernmost islands and nearby waters since a political dispute that erupted in November 2025 over a remark by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
Takaichi told a Japanese House of Representatives committee session that month that a Chinese naval blockade or armed conflict involving Taiwan could constitute a “survival-threatening situation” for her own country not far away. China claims self-ruled Taiwan as its own and has not ruled out the use of force to take it.
“There is a direct link between Takaichi’s statement and the quality and quantity of deployments,” said Stephen Nagy, a visiting fellow with the Japan Institute for International Affairs think tank in Tokyo. “(China) is also sending a signal to Tokyo that if it continues its current position vis-a-vis Taiwan that Beijing will continue these activities.”
China is using the deployments, including live-fire drills, uncrewed drone missions and voyages by entire aircraft carrier groups, to exert an unrelenting, long-term pressure on Japan without violating international maritime laws, analysts said.
“By repeatedly transiting waters around the (southwestern) Islands, China is gradually normalizing PLA Navy activity within the first island chain, expanding its operational experience and creating a pattern of accepted presence,” said Katsuya Yamamoto, director of the Tokyo-based Sasakawa Peace Foundation’s strategy and deterrence program.
The first island chain includes Japan, Taiwan and the Philippines.
“In other words, it is establishing facts on the ground, or rather at sea, that broaden its future freedom of action,” Yamamoto said.
In the seven weeks after Takaichi’s comment, the U.S. think tank Center for Strategic and International Studies logged a spike in “notable” PLA escalatory moves. Over 2025 overall, it said, China showed just a “slight increase” in the number of PLA naval vessels reported operating in waters around Japan, including an increase in the number of Chinese ships within the contiguous zone of the disputed Senkaku Islands, which China calls the Diaoyu.
Deployments near the uninhabited, Japanese-controlled Senkakus have “remained at very high levels” over the past year as before, while joint Sino-Russian missions around Japan and Chinese naval activity near the outlying Japanese islets around the Miyako Island “seem to have increased”, said Jeffrey Kingston, a professor specializing in Asian studies and history at Temple University, Japan Campus.
Chinese and Russian aircraft patrolled in June over the Sea of Japan, followed by a joint naval passage in July in the Miyako Strait near outlying Japanese islets. Chinese and Russian surveillance aircraft did five separate flights near Japan in October.
Spokespeople for the Chinese ministries of foreign affairs and national defense have called China’s military actions fair, valid and peaceful.
China is probably using military moves as one in a series of measures – some economic – to get back at Takaichi for her November 2025 remarks, Kingston said. “They haven’t forgotten, that’s for sure,” he said. “They are in various ways trying to put the screws on her.”
Officials in Beijing still want a retraction of the prime minister’s November 2025 comments but it’s unlikely, Kingston believes.
The Japanese government has verbally protested against Chinese military moves, tracked Chinese ships with its own, and scrambled fighter jets.
Tokyo is now considering a 70 trillion to 80 trillion yen (as high as $508 billion) defense spending plan for the five-year period beginning in April 2027, up from 43 trillion yen in the previous half-decade span, Japanese media outlets have reported.
“As the security environment becomes increasingly severe, cooperation with the ally and like-minded countries is indispensable to peace and stability in the region,” Japan’s Ministry of Defense said in an Oct. 29 statement after a meeting with defense officials from Australia, the Philippines and the United States.
The ministry, it said, “will continue to take advantage of various opportunities to further strengthen such cooperation.”

articles.title_orig: The Nvidia scandal fuels tougher China chip rules as Commerce targets Singapore and Malaysia
articles.title_zh: The Nvidia scandal fuels tougher China chip rules as Commerce targets Singapore and Malaysia
articles.content_orig:
The Commerce Department announced Monday it is cracking down on a loophole that has allowed Chinese firms to skirt export controls on American AI chips.
It marks the first government response since Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from his multitrillion-dollar chipmaker after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy — and as romances with at least two Nvidia employees surfaced.
The department’s Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule that seeks to close a loophole that Chinese firms have used to lease Nvidia’s advanced computing power by going through data centers in third countries, according to a Monday press release .
It was “written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council,” according to the release.
It came after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized the Commerce Department for not acting sooner against Megaspeed — an Nvidia customer for whom Huang lover Alice Huang, no relation, worked –which has been accused of illegally diverting sensitive AI chips to China.
A license will now “be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs) – countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion,” according to the new rule .
Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned President Trump about the former Nvidia boss’ romance with Alice Huang last spring, according to reports. Last week, Jensen Huang resigned following bombshell revelations about that relationship and an affair with senior Nvidia exec Kimberly Powell.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s team for the Chinese spy mess, saying the Treasury, State Department, Defense Department and US Trade Representative had been trying “for months” to blacklist Megaspeed.
In a Sunday letter addressed to Lutnick, Sen. Maria Cantwell of Washington – the top Dem on the Senate commerce committee – urged the commerce secretary to reinforce export controls on the sale of AI chips to China.
Chinese firms like Alibaba and ByteDance have “used overseas data centers equipped with advanced Nvidia chips to train advanced AI models,” she wrote. “These companies are exploiting a loophole in US export controls by using advanced American chips in foreign data centers even when those chips are restricted from the [People’s Republic of China].
“Despite warnings from the Bureau of Industry and Security that certain arrangements may violate existing restrictions, the Department of Commerce failed to close this loophole, allowing PRC companies to advance their AI capabilities using sensitive American technology.”
Asked about reports that Rubio had briefed Trump on the alleged Chinese spy plot targeting Huang, the president said Monday, “I haven’t heard that.”
“I don’t know that she [Alice Huang] is a spy,” the commander-in-chief told reporters as he left the White House for a trip to the Philippines and China. “Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she’s a spy.”
Trump also said that the national security of the country “was not put at risk” and that he “would not mind” if Huang was reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO.
Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been named as interim CEO , and the chipmaking giant has hired an outside firm to seek a permanent replacement.
With Huang, one of the driving forces of the AI boom, missing in action, investors have been panicking that Nvidia’s dealmaking could slow — a potentially massive monkey wrench for the sector after recent weeks have seen Wall Street get jittery about the tech trade.

articles.title_orig: Cantwell calls out U.S. Secretary of Commerce for allowing China access to advanced AI technology
articles.title_zh: Cantwell calls out U.S. Secretary of Commerce for allowing China access to advanced AI technology
articles.content_orig:
Sen. Maria Cantwell , the top Democrat on the Senate commerce committee, alleged in a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Sunday that the department under his leadership failed to prevent China from accessing the U.S.'s most advanced artificial intelligence chips.
In the letter, Cantwell prodded Lutnick to enforce export controls and stop the flow of AI chips to companies barred from receiving the technology. She sent the missive ahead of a planned meeting this week between U.S. officials and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, in China.
Her urging comes as Washington reels from revelations that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang. Nvidia is the leading U.S. company designing advanced AI chips.
Alice Huang was an executive at Singaporean technology company Megaspeed that allegedly smuggled restricted chips to China.
Lutnick, meanwhile, has come under fire for stalling efforts to crack down on chip sales to China and for his close personal relationship with Jensen Huang, who was a vocal opponent of export controls.
"The Department of Commerce has resisted efforts to restrict companies flagged as national security threats, weakened safeguards, and left open pathways for the PRC to train advanced AI models using sensitive American technology," Cantwell wrote to Lutnick. "These failures to carry out the law help give away America's technology advantage in AI."
The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Monday.
Cantwell called on Lutnick to use his authority to enforce a 2018 law, known as the Export Control Reform Act , which gives the Commerce Department broad latitude to enforce export controls and protect sensitive American technology.
She also cites potential financial conflicts involving Lutnick's sons , who control Cantor Fitzgerald, which she said held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock at the time of his nomination. And she notes the Trump administration's 25% fee on certain Nvidia chips sold to China, which she said could create "a perverse financial incentive to approve exports of sensitive American technology."
"America's national security and AI leadership cannot be compromised by family business interests or a policy that generates federal revenue from exporting technology critical to our competitive edge," Cantwell wrote.
Both Democratic and Republican members of Congress have ramped up pressure on Lutnick and other Commerce Department officials after a Nov. 9 New York Times report alleging the department may have slow-walked an investigation into Megaspeed.
On Thursday, Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott , R-S.C., summoned both Huang and Lutnick t o testify before his committee in December.
Lutnick has agreed to appear before the panel, Kristen Eichamer, a Commerce Department spokesperson, said in a statement last week.
And Democrats, who will take control of both the House and Senate in January, have signaled they will investigate Jensen Huang and Commerce officials.
On Wednesday, Sen. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., the top Democrat on the Senate banking panel, and Sen. Chris Coons , D-Del., the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations subpanel with jurisdiction over East Asia and the Pacific, sent a letter to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller instructing them to preserve all documents and communications related to Nvidia's exports of "advanced AI chips to China or to entities that may divert such chips to China."
The letter gives all three officials until Nov. 17 to confirm that preservation directives have been issued.

articles.title_orig: Trump Administration Moves to Close A.I. Chip Loophole Ahead of China Trip
articles.title_zh: Trump Administration Moves to Close A.I. Chip Loophole Ahead of China Trip
articles.content_orig:
The Trump administration said on Monday that it was moving forward with a new rule that would clamp down on China’s ability to access advanced A.I. chips through the use of data centers outside China’s borders.
The rule aims to close what many in Washington see as a loophole allowing China to sidestep a ban that prevents Chinese firms from buying the most advanced A.I. chips made by companies like Nvidia. Chinese firms have continued to legally access the chips by renting them from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere. Whether to close the loophole has been a significant source of contention within the Trump administration.
The new rule is intended to make it harder for Chinese firms to remotely access the chips. It will require chip sellers like Nvidia to obtain a license to sell advanced chips to overseas data centers that supply “significant volumes of computing power” to firms with headquarters in a small group of high-risk countries, a list that includes China, Russia and Iran.
Data centers are also required to perform strict checks on their customers to determine if they are linked to those countries. And the U.S. will now require a license to export advanced chips to companies with headquarters in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Brazil, which have a higher than normal risk of smuggling, the administration said.
The provision, which goes into effect in 90 days, will “undermine” the ability of companies in those countries from using U.S. chips to train advanced A.I. models, the administration said in a news release.
The plan to crack down on China’s ability to access the coveted A.I. chips comes as President Trump is scheduled to travel to Asia. He will travel to the Philippines and then to China for an economic summit, where he is expected to meet with the Chinese leader, Xi Jinping and discuss the war in Iran, nuclear nonproliferation and trade. The data center rules could create a new source of friction between the countries, at a time when Mr. Trump has been trying to keep a fragile trade truce with China intact.

articles.title_orig: After claiming election stolen, Netanyahu allies face their own meddling allegations
articles.title_zh: After claiming election stolen, Netanyahu allies face their own meddling allegations
articles.content_orig:
Two Israeli opposition leaders denounced an "attempted coup" on Monday following press reports that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month's election.
"As more and more details come to light, it becomes clear: This wasn't an attempt to disrupt the elections. It was an attempted coup," Yair Lapid, who headed the opposition in the previous legislature and co-chairs the Beyachad list, wrote on X.
Israel's Channel 12 television reported on Sunday that on the eve of the 27 October election, Netanyahu's chief of staff Ido Norden had phoned in a complaint to the police about members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party.
Norden reportedly pointed the police to a purported intelligence source, a former employee of Netanyahu's office, who provided information that led to the arrest of three Raam members.
The three men were later released when the police determined that the information was unfounded.
Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats. His Likud party issued a statement denying the latest allegations.
The Israeli newspaper Haaretz also reported that David Zini, head of the Shin Bet domestic security service, sought to wiretap leaders of the other Arab slate, the Joint List, but the attorney general turned down his request due to lack of evidence.
Following the report, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen also denounced an "attempted coup by Netanyahu".
"If the findings are confirmed, this is a criminal mechanism that operated from the heart of government to rig the election results. Everyone found responsible must be held accountable, including Netanyahu," he wrote on X.
Raam's number two, former police chief Yoav Segalovitz, called for an urgent investigation.
"These suspicions require an immediate, independent and thorough criminal investigation that reaches everyone involved, at every level and in every role," he wrote on X.
"Netanyahu cried out that his election was being stolen, while he himself tried to steal the country and is still trying to do so now," he added.
Netanyahu's main rival, former army chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, wrote on Sunday that the caretaker prime minister "cannot remain at the head of the government for a minute longer".
Neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Eisenkot's opposition secured the 61 seats required to form a government following last month's election.
The two Arab parties, the Joint List and Raam, have indicated support for Eisenkot who was tasked by President Isaac Herzog with forming a government.

articles.title_orig: Stocks Fall Before Nvidia Earnings, Anthropic IPO: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Stocks Fall Before Nvidia Earnings, Anthropic IPO: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
U.S. equities fell on Monday, dragged down by key technology stocks, as traders awaited a highly anticipated earnings report from Nvidia and a potentially record-setting public market debut of Anthropic this week.
The Nasdaq Composite declined 1.7%, while the S&P 500 fell 1.3%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 401 points, or 0.8%.
Shares in Nvidia were down more than 2%. On Monday, the Commerce Department moved to close a loophole that has let Chinese firms rent the chipmaker's computing power located in other countries. Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent over the weekend called for a " dramatic shakeup " at Nvidia, urging its board to look outside the company for its next CEO.
The embattled chipmaker is preparing to report its third-quarter results after the bell on Tuesday. While analysts expect the company to post nearly 100% year-over-year earnings and revenue growth, investors will be more focused on how the company will move forward after Jensen Huang's exit as chief executive.
Huang last week resigned from his post after reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia shares dropped 13%, marking their biggest weekly slide since April 2025.
"The main task at hand for interim CEO Colette Kress [is to] restore order and give the Street confidence in the Nvidia story going forward," wrote Dan Ives, analyst at Yorkville Ives. "This starts with earnings and the conference call this week on Tuesday after the bell…we still expect guidance and a typical conference call around robust business metrics with demand metrics that have clearly accelerated since last quarter."
Other stocks linked to the artificial intelligence trade were under pressure along with Nvidia. Fellow chipmakers Micron Technology , Intel and Advanced Micro Devices lost 6%, nearly 7% and 5%, respectively. Memory chip name Sandisk pulled back about 7%. Additionally, shares of computer maker Dell Technologies also declined about 6%, while software stock Oracle moved down 4%.
Another key test for the trade this week is Anthropic's initial public offering . The AI giant is eyeing a roughly $1.4 trillion valuation, with shares expected to be priced between $70 and $78.
Northcoast Research downgraded Costco Wholesale to neutral from buy on Monday after the stock's run higher this year.
The wholesale club has shown "remarkable success" as inflation drove shoppers into its stores, analyst Chuck Cerankosky said. However, shares currently trade at 48.4 times earnings.
"At multiples comparable to those of tech stocks and the rate at which the company is growing earnings, we believe shares of Costco Wholesale are valued fairly," he wrote in a note to clients.
The stock, which has gained 29% year to date, hit a 52-week high on Monday.
Despite uncertainty about the future of chipmaker Nvidia's leadership, there's strength ahead for semiconductors, according to Trivariate Research.
The firm expects "strong" earnings results from Nvidia this week and from memory maker Micron next month, supporting positive trends in returns over the next year.
"We think Semiconductors have a reasonable chance of being 50% higher in a year," Adam Parker at Trivariate wrote in a Sunday analysis.
Shares of Nvidia bounced on Thursday but failed to build on that progress on Friday, leading analysts at Wolfe to reconsider the $150 support level maintained last week.
"The stock successfully held that key $150 support level, after Thursday's notable intraday reversal. Unfortunately, the stock failed to build off of that reversal on Friday. Should price end up losing it, the next major support level sits around $100," Rob Ginsberg at Wolfe wrote in a Sunday note.
Bitcoin fell to its lowest levels since August over the weekend as a wave of forced liquidations accelerated amid broader weakening in market liquidity and risk appetite.
The price of the flagship cryptocurrency fell as low as $62,000 late Saturday, according to Coin Metrics, and is coming off its sixth weekly decline in a row. On Monday morning, it had climbed back to the $64,000 level.
Read the full story here .
The three major averages kicked off the first trading session of the week in the red.
The Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.4% just after 9:30 a.m. ET, while the S&P 500 declined 0.8%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 78 points, or 0.2%.
The Commerce Department moved on Monday to close a loophole that has let Chinese companies lease Nvidia 's advanced computing power from data centers in third countries, effectively circumventing controls on sensitive technology being exported to China .
Commerce's action, an interim final rule issued by its Bureau of Industry and Security, is the first U.S. policy response to the scandal at Nvidia that led CEO Jensen Huang to resign last week.
The department, in a press release, said that the BIS rule was "written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council." Read more .
Factory activity eased in  New York State during November though employment expanded at the fastest pace in more than four years, the regional Federal Reserve reported Monday.
The New York Fed's Empire State Manufacturing Index posted a reading of 7.8, down 18 points from October and below the Dow Jones consensus for 16.7. The index measures the difference between companies reporting growth against contraction, so a positive number still represents expansion.
Much of the decline came in new orders, which fell 20.2 points to 3.0. However, the employment index jumped to 18.1, growth of 7.8 points and its highest since June 2022. Prices also continued to climb but at a slower pace as the prices paid index fell 14 points to 45.9.
Nvidia continues to lose its luster, with two more Wall Street analysts lowering their price targets on the stock following a scandal that led to Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO.
Mizuho, which has an outperform on the chipmaker, lowered its price target on shares to $220 from $250. That still suggests 35% upside from Friday's close. UBS has a buy rating on the stock. It revised its price target on shares down to $240 from $300, which is 47% above the level at which Nvidia last closed.
"We believe ex-CEO Jensen was viewed as the global dealmaker 'AI banker', and key innovator," Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh said in a note to clients. "The significant NVDA ~32% stock decline from the Oct peak (vs. the SOX down 23%), reflects the 'Jensen/founder' premium lost. We believe the CEO departure also adds a 6-7-month management overhang, as [the] company comes under the US gov't microscope."
CNBC Pro subscribers can read more here .
Check out CNBC's live blog here for more on the stocks making premarket moves.
— Ananya Chetia and Fred Imbert
UniCredit 's takeover of Commerzbank has been given the go-ahead by European competition regulators.
The European Commission on Monday gave antitrust approval to the Italian lender's bid to take control of its German peer, following similar consent from the European Central Bank last month.
That now clears the path for the takeover, with UniCredit's integration plan expected to begin early next year.
"Our approval of UniCredit's acquisition of Commerzbank shows that it is possible to support a stronger European banking sector while safeguarding competition and choice," said Teresa Ribera, the Commission's first executive vice-president for a clean, just and competitive transition.
Shares in Milan-listed UniCredit were 0.62% lower in morning trade. Commerzbank was down 1% in Frankfurt.
Nvidia 's stock fell 1.72% in premarket trading, continuing its slide after losing hundreds of billions in market cap last week amid the fallout from Jensen Huang resigning as CEO.
Nvidia announced Huang was stepping down as CEO on Thursday, amid reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a spy for China. Huang told employees he had an affair in an email on Nov. 8.

articles.title_orig: Airstrikes on Iran Missile Sites May Shed Light on Justification for Dams
articles.title_zh: Airstrikes on Iran Missile Sites May Shed Light on Justification for Dams
articles.content_orig:
Environmentalists have long been mystified by the significant proliferation of dams and water transfer projects like pipelines and tunnels across Iran, especially in regions that had no apparent need for them.
Some analysts think they now know the answer after U.S. and Israeli airstrikes on concealed Iranian missile sites this year targeted many of the same areas. These analysts have concluded that the water projects may have been developed to support the country’s military buildup.
Given the secrecy surrounding Iran’s missile program, any connection between it and Iran’s ambitious, decades-old initiative to develop water infrastructure remains speculative. But some experts find the evidence highly suggestive.
Nima Shokri, an expert on water security, and his team at the Hamburg University of Technology, in Germany, had for years tracked an unusually high number of dams across Iran — at least 533 of them, among the most of any country in the region.
“It was always puzzling to me,” he said. “Why were they building so many dams?”
In the spring, Dr. Shokri was perusing news about the war in his home country when he came across a map plotting airstrikes that had targeted suspected military sites. The pattern — a semicircle of dots from north to south — nearly matched that of his own map marking the locations of dams.
His old question, he said, was superseded by a new one: “Why does it seem that wherever we have dams, there is a missile strike close by?”

articles.title_orig: Russell Brand prison message 'appalling' and being investigated, No 10 says
articles.title_zh: Russell Brand prison message 'appalling' and being investigated, No 10 says
articles.content_orig:
A message by Russell Brand to his followers in which he claimed innocence for his sexual offences was "clearly appalling" and is being urgently investigated, Downing Street has said.
The comedian is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
His wife Laura read out a message from him on their Sunday Service show on YouTube, in which the convicted rapist claimed: "I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for."
No 10 said it expects action to be taken if Brand is found to have broken prison rules.
Victims' commissioner for London Andrea Simon said the claims will "certainly retraumatise his victims and other survivors of rape who have to hear it".
In the couple's podcast, released on Sunday, Laura Brand can be seen sitting on a sofa and is holding a Bible with a candle burning in front of her.
Relaying the message from her husband, Laura Brand said the comedian - who is currently being held at HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire - called prison staff "strong", "kind" and "dedicated", and asked people to support his "treasured wife and family".
She said she had been speaking to him and he "is OK and is praying".
Brand has positioned himself as a Christian influencer, and has a large following among believers, including in the US.
Asked about the message, the prime minister's official spokesman said: "Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances.
"Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments."
Speaking earlier, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Sky News: "His crimes are heinous and awful. I think it's revolting, by the way, that he shows no remorse today in his comments."
"No remorse, no sympathy for the victims. Just disgusting comments," he added.
Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, victim's commissioner for London Andrea Simon added: "The victims during the sentencing hearing highlighted how his denials and ongoing media fame over two decades had added to their pain and trauma," she said.
"The fact survivors are still having to hear this now is really problematic and very concerning that we can't do more to protect them from it."
While freedom of expression allows convicted sex offenders such as Brand to profess their innocence, Simon said terms of service of media platforms should regulate "the way in which they get their message out".
She added that prison rules should also be reviewed to "bar those convicted of sending messages to be broadcast" unless permission is granted by the prison governor.
If Brand is found to have broken prison rules, possible punishments enforceable by prison governors can result in restrictions on social visits or loss of privileges such as access to additional time in the gym or loss of TV.
Governors can also impose proportionate restrictions on communications where justified.
This could include blocking specific phone numbers, increased monitoring of calls or restricting contact with individuals where necessary to protect victims or maintain prison security.
Over the weekend, Brand was moved from the category B HMP Wandsworth in south London to the category C HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire, a prison that mostly houses sex offenders and has tailored programmes for them.
Foreign Office minister Stephen Doughty, told LBC he agreed it was not "a good look" that he'd been moved to a lower security prison.
"I think people want to see him facing the appropriate punishment for what are appalling crimes against women and others and I think the whole episode is shocking," he said.
Meanwhile, there have been calls for a change in the law following Brand's conviction so that sexual relationships between 16 and 17-year-olds and adults would be illegal. The government says a discussion is to take place.
Mia Latter, who has alleged she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16, is among those campaigning for ministers to introduce a staggered age of consent.
She was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation. Brand denied the allegations at the time. None of the women were complainants in his recent criminal trial.
Latter, who was known under the pseudonym "Alice" in the 2023 investigation, has now waived her right to anonymity.
In an interview with LBC on Monday, Latter said: "We don't want to criminalise anybody under the age of 18 [including] 16, 17-year-olds, 18-year-olds having sex with each other...
"I think healthy relationships are important, and they're important in helping you develop and grow."
But she said there should be an age "threshold" for the partners of 16 and 17 year-olds.
Layla Stone, founder of the campaign group Close the Consent Gap, is urging a change in the law to prevent 16 year-olds from having a sexual relationship with anyone older than 19, and someone aged 17 from having a relationship with anyone older than 20.
She told BBC Breakfast that "predators know exactly what they are doing".
Asked about the issue on BBC Breakfast, the foreign secretary said: "I think the reason why it's right to have this debate is we've seen some of the very, very brave victims of Russell Brand come forward and say 'we think this needs looking at'".
Shadow education secretary Laura Trott said she is glad there is a conversation around staggering the age of consent but warned that it had "been quite complicated to actually implement" in some US states where it is used.
Trott said a suggestion that the age of consent should be raised to 18 is also a "conversation we need to have" but "probably isn't practical".
Anna Edmundson, director of policy & social change at the NSPCC charity, said: "We urgently need a review of what is and isn't working to ensure 16 and 17-year-olds are fully protected in law from this predatory behaviour.
"However, closing these gaps will only be part of the solution. We must question why adults have been able to exploit teenagers in plain sight for so long, and look at what further action is needed to help people recognise the signs of exploitation."
Any change in the law would only affect England and Wales as Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate legislative powers in relation to the age of consent, which is also currently set at 16 in both nations.
The Scottish Government said it had "no current plans" to change the age of consent, following the calls by campaigners, but any proposals would be considered.
The foreign secretary also apologised for having appeared on Russell Brand's online show in 2015, when he was Labour leader.
Miliband told Today if he'd known about the allegations then, he would not have done spoken to him, adding: "I deeply regret doing that interview and all my sympathies are with those victims."

articles.title_orig: Nvidia set to deliver first life-after-Huang briefing
articles.title_zh: Nvidia set to deliver first life-after-Huang briefing
articles.content_orig:
The largest technology stocks linked to the artificial intelligence trade could stand to benefit the most from Nvidia's woes and a Democratic-controlled Congress pushing back on data centers, according to investing experts interviewed on CNBC's " ETF Edge " earlier this week.
"We may have been put in an environment, as much as investors have sort of been looking for areas outside of Big Tech, where net-net Big Tech ends up as the winner once again," said Roundhill Investments CEO Dave Mazza, whose firm manages the Magnificent Seven ETF ( MAGS ).
Part of his bull case: Other players in the AI trade are positioned to fill Nvidia's chip demand if investors lose trust in the company after a tumultuous week that saw its iconic founder and CEO Jensen Huang resign.
"If we get into an environment where people can't trust … Nvidia, they're going to look for other sources for these chips because they need them," Mazza said during the "ETF Edge" interview, which occurred Monday as the Nvidia scandal grew but before Huang had resigned.
Discussing recent fund flow activity for the MAGS ETF, as well as for the Roundhill Neocloud ETF ( NCLD ) — which focuses on smaller market cap, specialized cloud computing companies — Mazza said, "In a weird way, [hyperscalers] may continue to benefit from this because they have the compute available. It's going to be more valuable if the demand is there."
The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF ended the week in the green, albeit with a gain of less than 1%, while the Roundhill Neocloud ETF was up over 1%, though earnings from top holdings Coreweave and Nebius presented a mixed picture.
CoreWeave had its best day since April 2025 on Wednesday after its latest quarterly results, while Nebius shares sank after its Thursday report. The neocloud ETF remains deeply in the red since its August 2026 launch, down 39%, amid concerns about balance sheet strength, which could linger given Nvidia's role in financing the AI buildout. CoreWeave shares sank again on Friday, and Nvidia posted its longest losing streak since 2012 after its latest weekly losses.
Nvidia's interim CEO and current chief financial officer Colette Kress will have her first opportunity to reassure the market when Nvidia reports its third-quarter earnings next Tuesday. "Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders," Kress said in a statement issued on Thursday morning when the company announced Huang's exit.
Yorkville Ives partner and senior managing director Dan Ives said on "ETF Edge" on Monday that the market will remain optimistic about other AI chip players, like AMD and Alphabet, if Nvidia faces prolonged headwinds. Ives helped create the Dan IVES Wedbush AI Revolution ETF ( IVES ) while at Wedbush Securities, where he served as the managing director and global head of technology research before departing Wedbush to form his own firm earlier this year.
AMD finished trading this week up close to 13%, with Broadcom posting similar gains.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq index posted its best week since August as Nvidia's slump reshuffled the AI trade.
Yorkville Ives lowered its price target on Nvidia to $225 from $300 on Thursday after Huang's resignation, but maintained a buy rating on the stock, which finished the week at $162.85 per share.
"Nvidia remains the clear leader in GPU chips for the AI Revolution. They are roughly 2-3 years ahead of the nearest competitor and the demand trajectory the next few years is not changing because Jensen is gone," Ives wrote in a note to investors on Thursday. "The strategic roadmap is already essentially built around the next few family of chips and physical AI with 42k employees driving it. ... Valuation at roughly 10x 28 EPS is way too cheap once Nvidia gets through this storm and emerges on the other side."
The compute that does exist could become even more indispensable against the backdrop of a potential slowdown to the data-center buildout by Congress after the Democratic Party gains of Nov. 3 swept control of Congress, Mazza said.
Ives estimates that the "blue tidal wave" in Congress could mean 10% of planned data centers won't materialize on the low end, and 15%-20% on the high end, but he added that demand still outstrips supply four to one. "The compute is just that much more valuable in the capacity today than it was a week ago. So I could argue just more and more bullish, strong, get stronger," Ives said.
"The game is going to change for Big Tech. It will slow it down. But there's no overbuild, no bubble concerns. And I view that as actually a positive thing," he added.

articles.title_orig: Novo says Wegovy injection lowers BMI and obesity rates in children in trial
articles.title_zh: Novo says Wegovy injection lowers BMI and obesity rates in children in trial
articles.content_orig:
Novo on Monday released full results from a late-stage trial showing its blockbuster Wegovy injection helped children ages 6 to under 12 with obesity shed weight, significantly lowering their body mass index.
Wegovy reduced BMI by an estimated 19.7 percentage points on average compared with a placebo at 68 weeks, with BMI falling 17.4% among children receiving the drug and rising 2.2% among those receiving a placebo. Those results assumed patients stayed on treatment during the trial.
When evaluating all children in the study, including those who discontinued treatment, Wegovy lowered BMI by an estimated average of 16.2 percentage points more than the placebo at 68 weeks. All 167 kids in the study received lifestyle modifications throughout the trial, including a ​reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.
The detailed results mark an encouraging step forward in treating childhood obesity — a chronic disease that can carry serious cardiovascular, metabolic and psychosocial consequences but has had few treatment options for younger children. When left unaddressed, childhood obesity can extend into adulthood, bringing earlier and more severe health complications.
"This is a very significant disease burden in this very young patient population," said Dr. Andrea Traina, Novo's medical director lead of obesity.
In 2025, the disease affected an estimated roughly 177 million children and teens ages 5 to 19 worldwide, according to the World Obesity Federation. That figure is projected to rise to 228 million by 2040.
While Wegovy is already approved to treat obesity in children ages 12 and older, there are currently no approved medications for those under 12. The latest results offer evidence that Wegovy can potentially fill that treatment gap, safely and effectively reducing the severity of the disease in children as young as 6.
In Novo's trial, 85% of children started with moderate to severe obesity, which corresponds to BMI thresholds of 35 and above and 40 or higher, respectively. Nearly half already had at least one obesity-related complication, such as high blood pressure, high cholesterol or sleep apnea.
But more than 40% of children treated with Wegovy were no longer classified as having obesity after 68 weeks of the trial, assuming patients stayed on treatment. Novo initially shared that result in September.
"We are driving towards control of this chronic disease in that patient population when they are still so young and at such high risk for more advanced and accelerated disease progression because they developed it so early," Traina said.
Novo said Wegovy's overall safety and tolerability among children — how well patients managed the drug — were consistent with those seen in ​trials ⁠with adults. The company added that it observed no safety concerns related to growth or pubertal development in the kids.
Still, the two-year study does not establish whether treating obesity earlier can change its long-term trajectory, or what treatment and maintenance might look like as children grow into adulthood, Traina said.
"That is something that is still an evidence gap," she said, pointing to the potential of future research.

articles.title_orig: Bitcoin slides to $62,000 following liquidation cascade, then rebounds slightly
articles.title_zh: Bitcoin slides to $62,000 following liquidation cascade, then rebounds slightly
articles.content_orig:
Bitcoin fell to its lowest levels since August over the weekend as a wave of forced liquidations accelerated amid broader weakening in market liquidity and risk appetite.
The price of the flagship cryptocurrency fell as low as $62,000 late Saturday, according to Coin Metrics, and is coming off its sixth weekly decline in a row. On Monday morning, it had climbed back to the $64,000 level.
Bitcoin's ongoing weakness pushed its price below key technical support levels during the week, breaking below its 200-day moving average of about $73,000 and triggering the cascade of long liquidations, forcing traders to sell their assets at market price to settle their debts, pushing prices lower.
On Saturday night, exchanges tracked by CoinGlass saw more than $165 million in liquidated bitcoin long positions, following $629 million on Friday and nearly $700 million on Thursday.
Bitcoin was also facing potential selling pressure ahead of Anthropic's anticipated initial public offering, with the listing drawing speculative capital away from riskier assets.
On Friday, the dollar index – which has an inverse relationship with bitcoin – reached its highest level since April 2025, following hotter-than-expected inflation earlier this week that increased expectations of further Fed tightening. That pushed Treasury yields and the dollar higher while pressuring both bitcoin and gold, despite their appeal as alternative stores of value in the longer term.
Throughout November, bitcoin has been struggling from the combination of dollar strength, institutional selling, and ongoing leveraged bitcoin liquidations. The declines began in late October, as concerns over artificial intelligence valuations and spending fueled a broad tech sell-off. They were compounded by the $6.3 billion Binance hack and weakening institutional ETF demand.
Bitcoin's next critical test is between $60,000 and $62,000, according to Nicolai Sondergaard, a research analyst at Nansen.
"A break below $60,000 is possible if Nvidia's results add to the tech selling," he said. "The catalysts for a move higher are mostly macro, and a softer dollar with falling real yields would ease the pressure on every risk asset at once. If that happens, bitcoin goes into the recovery with less leverage than it carried in October, and a close back above $73,000 would be the first sign that the selling is over."
Edwin Mata, CEO of tokenization platform Brickken, said he's monitoring whether spot buyers step in once the forced selling subsides.
"Clearing out leveraged longs can slow the selling," he said. "For a recovery to hold, spot buyers need to keep showing up after the forced selling has passed."

articles.title_zh: Nvidia can replace Jensen Huang, but not the handshakes behind its chips: Chart of the Day
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
A Jensen Huang comeback is a 1-in-9 long shot on prediction markets, and Dan Ives calls it "ridiculous." Nvidia's ( NVDA ) supply chain, built on his handshakes, makes it less ridiculous than it sounds.
Days after Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid affair scandals, the Financial Times reported Sunday that he has discussed a return, and allies are building a Silicon Valley "war room" to lobby the board.
Nvidia stock is on track for its lowest close since early July 2025, about a third below its October record. The company's first earnings report without Huang comes Tuesday after the market close.
Yorkville's Ives said "no one individual can replace Jensen as CEO," but he called a comeback "ridiculous in our view given the legal/Board/DC scrutiny/moral compass/China tentacles."
The case for Huang starts with paperwork that doesn't exist. He has said Nvidia has never signed a contract with chipmaker TSMC ( TSM ) in three decades of business. Elon Musk, who backs a petition to bring Huang back, wrote on X that many deals "were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract" and that "without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."
The scale is staggering. One Vera Rubin rack, Nvidia's newest AI system, holds 1.3 million parts, per the company's count, from a supply chain twice the size of the one behind Blackwell. More than 150 partners in Taiwan alone help build it.
Nvidia had lined up $279 billion in supply and capacity commitments as of July, according to its latest quarterly filing . That's 17 times the total in January 2024. About $267 billion comes due in the next 2.5 years, and some of those deals can be canceled or adjusted before firm orders are placed.
Bettors took notice. Polymarket odds that Huang takes any formal role at Nvidia by year-end nearly doubled to about 20% after the FT report, then drifted down to about 11% Monday morning.
Nvidia's own annual report warns it is "highly dependent on the services of our longstanding executive team." And Huang ran the company with about 60 direct reports.
"How can you have the world's most valuable company and no kind of succession plan, not even anyone being groomed, [and] 60 people reporting to Jensen?" former Medtronic chair and CEO Bill George told Yahoo Finance .
The board isn't rolling out the welcome mat for Huang. It has approached Arm ( ARM ) CEO Rene Haas about the job, the FT reported, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants a dramatic shake-up with an outside CEO.
Not everyone buys the indispensable-founder pitch. "I'm not Jensen … but I know how little of the actual work that I do," Cisco chair and CEO Chuck Robbins told Yahoo Finance, pointing to Nvidia's "42,000 employees that wake up every day and go to the office and do a great job."
Former Goldman Sachs CEO Lloyd Blankfein put it in historical terms on X: "Sad about Jensen. Shakespearean. But as de Gaulle said, 'The graveyards are filled with indispensable men.'"

articles.title_zh: Scores of Bahraini Shi'ite clerics get life in jail, accused of plotting with Iran
articles.content_orig:
Bahrain sentenced dozens of Shiite Muslim clerics and other religious figures to life in prison on terrorism charges on Monday, accusing them of colluding with Iran against the Bahraini government.
The convictions underscored rising sectarian and political tensions in Bahrain, a Gulf Arab country, amid the U.S.-Israeli war on Shiite-led Iran. Human rights groups had denounced the trial , saying that it was marred by allegations of torture and coerced confessions.
A lawyer for several of the defendants, speaking on condition of anonymity out of fear of retribution from Bahrain’s authoritarian government, said that all of them had pleaded not guilty. He described the trial as farcical, saying that lawyers had been deprived of basic information about the charges against their clients.
When asked about those claims, the Bahraini government said in a statement that all of the defendants had been “afforded their full legal rights and safeguards, including the right of defense,” and that complaints of mistreatment would be referred for investigation.
“This case was about criminal conduct, not faith or belief,” the government added.
The Bahraini authorities had accused the defendants of forming a “terrorist group” linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps of Iran. According to a statement from the Bahraini public prosecution department, published by the state news agency, the defendants had worked to undermine the Bahraini government, and the group’s leaders had received “assignments and instructions” from Iranian officials.
“They had also sought to change the system of government by force and unlawful means through incitement to commit terrorist acts, acts of rioting and sabotage,” the statement added.

articles.title_orig: Houthis seize ground on Yemen's southern coast, edge closer to Aden
articles.title_zh: Houthis seize ground on Yemen's southern coast, edge closer to Aden
articles.content_orig:
Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia say they are redeploying troops to defend the country's interim capital, Aden, following weeks of intensified fighting with the Iran-backed Houthi movement.
The Southern Armed Forces said it was withdrawing from an area overlooking the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, at the southern end of the Red Sea, to reinforce positions around Aden and neighbouring areas.
Houthi-run media say the movement has taken control of the evacuated territory. Saudi Arabia has not commented.
The shift ends a weeks-long offensive to try to secure the area near the key shipping route which the Houthis seized in a surprise offensive in September.
Pro-government forces said they had "secured" the strait in early October as they sought to retake crucial ground from the Houthis. The Iran-backed fighters said they had captured areas including Perim Island at the mouth of the strait and the strategic port city of Mokha a month prior.
But the Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces fighting on behalf of Yemen's internationally recognised government said on Sunday they were withdrawing to reinforce troops elsewhere, with the southern city of Aden a "priority".
It said troops were being withdrawn "from Dhubab Airport and the Bab al-Mandab area" with the aim of "strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats".
"This step is driven by the priority of securing the capital, Aden, and neighbouring governorates, reinforcing the front lines and addressing existing threats."
The Houthis said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway when they captured territory overlooking it, but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.
However, the seizure contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.
A UN Human Rights spokesperson, Ravina Shamdasani, urged all parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure.
She noted that since the escalation of fighting in August, more than 60% of documented civilian casualties were women and children.
The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Aden in recent weeks, including an assault on 15 October that targeted the presidential palace, killing five and injuring 16.
Saudi Arabia responded with hundreds of air strikes, while the Houthis launched hundreds of drones and missiles at its cities and infrastructure.
The UN has estimated that nearly 330,000 people have been displaced in Yemen as the fighting has since escalated. Hundreds of people are reported to have been killed.
Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from its capital, Sanaa.
The conflict escalated in 2015 after a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.
A four-year informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

articles.title_orig: Houthis edge closer to Aden as Yemeni forces pull out of Bab al-Mandeb
articles.title_zh: Houthis edge closer to Aden as Yemeni forces pull out of Bab al-Mandeb
articles.content_orig:
Forces aligned with the internationally recognised Yemeni government face a potentially catastrophic situation, as Houthi forces advance on the southern city of Aden and other strategic areas.
Yemeni government forces said on Sunday they had withdrawn from Dhubab airport and territory they held near the Bab al-Mandeb strait, southwest of Yemen, to defend Aden, the de facto seat of the government.
Retired Lebanese Brigadier-General Hassan Jouni, a military and strategic expert, said fighting is now focused on control over a mountainous triangle of territory in southern Yemen, which could decide the outcome of the war.
This area links Aden to Taiz, another city held by the government but encircled by the Houthis – an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God) – and Bab al-Mandeb, a maritime chokepoint that connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
“This triangle is the strategic centre of gravity for the war in Yemen as a whole,” Jouni told Al Jazeera.
On Sunday, government-aligned forces were withdrawn from Dhubab, which was recaptured from the Houthis in September, to avoid an imminent siege in the coastal strip by the Houthis and to help defend Aden, analysts say.
Houthi advances in this southwestern region now threaten to completely cut off the government’s coastal supply routes, Jouni said.
The Yemen war began when the Houthis, a Zaidi Shia group close to Iran, captured the capital, Sanaa, in September 2014, forcing the government to flee south to Aden. Saudi Arabia launched an Arab coalition military campaign to aid the government in March 2015, launching thousands of air strikes against Houthi forces.
Following a relatively peaceful few years, fighting re-erupted in July when government forces’ jets bombed Sanaa international airport to prevent a Houthi delegation from landing in the Yemeni capital.
A Houthi offensive in September saw the government lose control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, including the key port city of Mocha . Later Houthi advances also saw Taiz completely besieged by the Houthis.
Yemeni Armed Forces spokesperson Majed al-Nuzaili defended the retreat from Dhubab, saying it was part of a wider tactical manoeuvre.
“[The redeployment] is an extension of the heroic positions of the popular resistance and the southern forces in protecting the temporary capital Aden,” he said on X.
But Jouni believes the situation faced by government forces is grim, with the Houthis reaching Tor al-Baha, just 80km (50 miles) from Aden.
“The Houthi forces have reached this line, meaning that they are indeed in the defensive line area of the city of Aden. We do not say they have approached Aden, but the defence of the city of Aden begins in this area,” he told Al Jazeera.
“The basic combat direction now is in the vicinity of the besieged city of Taiz. On the other hand, of course, the Houthis will focus their attention now on approaching Aden and controlling the first defensive zone.”
Strategic affairs expert Ali al-Dahab gave a less optimistic assessment of the situation than the one presented by the government.
“What happened is a retreat or a withdrawal with the same meaning, and not a redeployment, because the withdrawal left a vast vacuum filled by the Houthis,” al-Dahab stated.
The government’s “Operation Yemen Dawn” has responded to the situation with a dramatic increase in strikes on Houthi positions, including 900 targeting operations within 24 hours.
The Houthis have responded with ballistic missiles and drone attacks towards Mecca, Riyadh, and the Eastern province in Saudi Arabia. They have announced they will continue operations under a principle of “siege for siege, airport for airport, and escalation for escalation”.
Al-Dahab said this strategy is directed at Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government’s key international ally, and not at authorities in Aden.
With their recent gains on the coast along Bab al-Mandeb, which has become increasingly significant to global maritime trade since the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the US-Israel war on Iran, the Houthis have significant geopolitical leverage.
“They now directly and completely control the western Yemeni coastal sector and part of the maritime extension towards Aden,” al-Dahab warned.
“The matter translates the Houthis’ gains in Bab al-Mandeb in large part to the benefit of Iran.”

articles.title_orig: Microsoft outage saw 80% of servers fail – here’s what happened
articles.title_zh: Microsoft outage saw 80% of servers fail – here’s what happened
articles.content_orig:
Last week saw a truly epic outage to Microsoft 365 , with a huge number of users unable to send and receive emails. The company has now admitted that at the worst point, more than 80% of its servers were unresponsive.
Microsoft has now explained what went wrong, stating that the mistake that led to the failure was actually made all the way back in July without being detected …
The company said at the time that it was a technical issue and not a cyber attack, and that it was working hard to fix the problem, admitting that it was taking longer than expected. Microsoft also denied that it was related to the thousands of layoffs announced the previous month.
Users were understandably unimpressed at the scale of the outage and the time taken to fix it, although meme creators were having fun.
Sorry but you have to be change the name now. Thems the rules pic.twitter.com/5UttZ8nt9f
It certainly points out that when you base your business on cloud services, you also take the risk that comes with that.
Platform head Charles Lamanna admitted the severity of the problem.
In less than two hours, the previously unknown defect was encountered across our fleet and rendered them unresponsive. At its lowest, more than 80% of servers were unresponsive.
He said it resulted from a combination of two issues. The company maintains two independent network gateway systems, one of which failed, meaning that the remaining gateway took the full load. That wouldn’t have been a problem on its own, Microsoft stating that each one has enough capacity to handle all traffic. However, a mistake made back in July led to a cascading failure.
A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions. This was due to lock contention inside an internal process which caused the machine to become unavailable. This defect was the result of a fix that was prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers […]
The initial change in behavior first started deployment in July of this year. The update went through safe deployment and saturated globally over several weeks, during which time no issues were observed. For more than three months, the change was deployed worldwide without impact. Our normal load testing did not detect the latent issue because the different traffic and SKU mix used in our test labs. The contention issue is worsened on machines with more cores and newer hardware; whereas our load testing tended to focus on our weaker hardware SKUs with fewer cores.
In other words, the update wasn’t tested under the conditions in which it was most likely to fail.
While the company claims that the incident is unrelated to laying off staff and replacing them with AI systems, I find myself extremely skeptical. It seems inconceivable that a company of Microsoft’s size could make what appears to be a schoolboy error of this magnitude unless there were insufficient engineers working on the update. articles.title_orig: Ukraine hits Kerch bridge between Russia and occupied Crimea
articles.title_zh: Ukraine hits Kerch bridge between Russia and occupied Crimea
articles.content_orig:
Traffic temporarily restricted on key connection after bridge targeted during overnight drone barrage by Ukraine
Ukraine has hit the Kerch bridge connecting occupied Crimea with Russia, in a symbolic blow that temporarily paralysed road traffic and left thousands of drivers stranded.
A Ukrainian kamikaze drone crashed into one of the bridge’s arches at 5.38am local time, local channels reported. Earlier drones could be heard buzzing above the structure, as Russian air defence units opened fire.
The extent of the damage was unclear. One report said the arch was listing at a 15-degree angle and “looked tired”.
The Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea , Sergey Aksyonov, confirmed the “enemy” had launched an attack. “As a result, traffic will be restricted, likely until the afternoon,” he wrote on Telegram.
Russian officials said the crossing would remain closed while experts assessed its condition. About 2,000 vehicles were reportedly stuck in traffic jams on both sides.
In a call with reporters, the Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, downplayed the incident. He said: “Minor damage is being assessed. ⁠Traffic across the bridge continues.”
Ukraine says the bridge is a legitimate target for its armed forces, and has made at least two previous attempts to blow it up.
In 2022 a truck laden with explosives damaged part of the road section. A second strike using a “sea baby” drone took place the following year. Russia has subsequently strengthened air defences and installed metal barges and boom barriers.
Overnight Ukraine launched 1,336 drones, in what the Kremlin says was one of the biggest attacks so far this year. About 600 were intercepted on their approach to Moscow, claimed the capital’s mayor, Sergei Sobyanin.
The barrage took place days before a summit in Shenzhen between China’s president, Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Putin. US officials say the talks will not focus on the war in Ukraine, where Russia’s military offensive has largely stalled.
after newsletter promotion
Ukraine says its retaliatory strikes are justified retribution for Russia’s own missile and drone barrages of its cities and energy grid – attacks that have killed hundreds of civilians and regularly knock out power and heating for millions. In recent weeks Russia has repeatedly hit two critical bridges in Kyiv over the Dnipro river.
Diplomatic efforts on ending the almost five-year war have so far gone nowhere. After a fresh round of talks in Abu Dhabi last week, Putin reiterated his hardline territorial demands and said any deployment of foreign troops would be seen in Moscow as a “continuation of war”.
The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , said on Friday the Trump administration had proposed that Kyiv gives Russia the eastern Donbas region – including towns and villages Russia does not control – in exchange for Nato membership or Nato-like guarantees.
Zelenskyy ruled out handing over territory. The details of possible US security guarantees were vague and did not feature American troops on the ground, he said, citing conversations with Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and the real-estate developer Steve Witkoff. The emissaries last week saw Putin in Moscow.

articles.title_orig: 'iPhone 20 Pro' Rumored to Be Based on iPhone Air
articles.title_zh: 'iPhone 20 Pro' Rumored to Be Based on iPhone Air
articles.content_orig:
Next year's "iPhone 20 Pro" models will use the same glass design as the iPhone Air , but with more pronounced curvature along all four sides, according to the leaker known as " Fixed Focus Digital ."
In a new post on Weibo, the leaker said the device would use the same glass material as the ‌iPhone Air‌, adjusted to have greater curvature and produce a four-sided curved effect. The accompanying hashtag refers specifically to an "iPhone 20 Pro" with a four-sided curved, "all-glass" design.
An illustration shared with the post depicts rounded front and rear glass meeting a narrow, polished, gold-colored metallic frame. Physical side buttons, antenna lines, and a protruding rear camera assembly remain visible.
Taken together with earlier rumors and the post's accompanying illustration, the repeated comparisons suggest a design somewhere between the iPhone X and ‌iPhone Air‌. The ‌iPhone Air‌ provides a reference for the slim profile and a more modern iPhone design, while the more pronounced glass curvature recalls the rounded edges of the iPhone X. Both feature a polished frame.
The latest claim builds on Fixed Focus Digital's previous report that Apple had modified ‌iPhone Air‌ manufacturing equipment to produce more rounded glass components for the 20th anniversary models. The leaker said the changes had helped reduce manufacturing costs, while substantially improving thinness and heat dissipation.
In a still-earlier report , the same leaker also claimed that a supply chain facility had completed renovations ahead of "iPhone 20" production, with manufacturing quality expected to be roughly comparable to the first-generation ‌iPhone Air‌. The ‌iPhone Air‌ features Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and Ceramic Shield on the back.
The broader design picture aligns with Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman 's reporting that Apple's anniversary Pro models will feature glass that curves into the sides from both the front and rear, with a thin metal band between the two panels. Gurman has also described thinner display bezels and curved glass around all corners and edges, in what he expects to be the biggest overhaul of the Pro line since the iPhone X.
Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone models are expected to launch in the fall of 2027 . While leakers have variably referred to the device as the "iPhone 20 Pro," Apple's naming plans remain unclear. It seems plausible that the company could skip the iPhone 19 name to emphasize the anniversary, similar to its introduction of the iPhone X in 2017.

articles.title_orig: Barristers must stop using rape myths in trials, justice secretary says
articles.title_zh: Barristers must stop using rape myths in trials, justice secretary says
articles.content_orig:
The justice secretary has called for new rules to prevent barristers from using rape myths to defend their clients in the wake of the Russell Brand trial.
As first reported by the Times , in a letter to the Bar Standards Board (BSB), Alex Norris said it was "unacceptable" to "perpetuate myths" about victims in court and disciplinary action could be taken against those who do so.
In his closing speech, Brand's defence barrister, Ian Winter KC, questioned why his client's accusers had not fought back.
The BSB said it had set up an expert group this year to advise on "strengthening standards for barristers", while the Bar Council said defendants had a "right to have evidence tested in court".
Brand was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
Winter said to the court "not one of them [Brand's accusers] resisted or screamed or even tried to leave".
Winter also asked the jury if they could be sure that out of the "many, many women" Brand had had sex with over a decade, "he raped just three of them".
Norris wrote in his letter to the BSB: "[The board] must send a strong signal to the profession on the harm arising from rape myths, and that the perpetuation of such myths within a court room is unacceptable, just as they are unacceptable in our society at large."
The charity Rape Crisis says it is "really common for people who experience rape, sexual assault, sexual abuse or other types of sexual violence to find they can't move or speak".
The judge presiding over Brand's case was praised by the Criminal Bar Association and campaign groups for comments he made during his sentencing remarks to dispel rape myths.
Mr Justice Bennathan told Southwark Crown Court: "Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no and to demand justice from the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent."
A spokesperson for the BSB said such cases "must be decided on the basis of the evidence and not prejudice", adding: "Any other approach may discourage others from coming forward and adversely affect public confidence in the criminal justice system more widely."
Kirsty Brimelow KC, chair of the Bar Council of England and Wales which is part of the group examining the need for further training, said it was important for the BSB to remain "independent of the government".
She told BBC Radio 4's Woman's Hour that a "regulatory gap" had not been made clear to her and there were already powers to discipline barristers if breaches of the code of conduct happen.
She said training for "vulnerable witnesses" was already undertaken but it could be "problematic" if it was made mandatory.
Brimelow said there were currently a lack of barristers defending cases of rape and sexual assault and the possibility of further compulsory training could see more pushed out.
"What I wouldn't like to see is publicity around one case to take a life of its own rather than looking at what we already do," she told the BBC.
A spokesperson for the Ministry of Justice said the justice secretary was "determined to make protections for victims as strong as possible".
"Rape myths have absolutely no place in our courts, giving evidence in cases of this nature is a brave act and can be traumatic for victims: they must never feel as though they are the ones on trial," the spokesperson said.
"Independent judges are already able to, and do, give directions to counter rape myths but we always want to keep looking at ways we can improve how the entire justice system treats victims of sexual violence."
In an interview with the BBC earlier this month, Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said some of the comments made at the trial he had seen reported were "getting very close to victim blaming".
He also backed calls for a law change that would require judges to direct juries on rape myths and misconceptions in every rape trial.
"It shouldn't be possible for inaccurate statements to be made to a jury to suggest that because a rape victim didn't behave in one way that somehow undermines their case," Sir Mark said.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the government needs to make sure victims of rape cases do not feel like they are on trial .

articles.title_zh: Bahrain Convicts Dozens of Shiite Clerics in Sweeping Terrorism Trial
articles.content_orig:
Bahrain sentenced dozens of Shiite Muslim clerics and other religious figures to life in prison on terrorism charges on Monday, accusing them of colluding with Iran against the Bahraini government.
The convictions underscored rising sectarian and political tensions in Bahrain, a Gulf Arab country, amid the U.S.-Israeli war on Shiite-led Iran. Human rights groups had denounced the trial , saying that it was marred by allegations of torture and coerced confessions.
A lawyer for several of the defendants, speaking on condition of anonymity out of fear of retribution from Bahrain’s authoritarian government, said that all of them had pleaded not guilty. He described the trial as farcical, saying that lawyers had been deprived of basic information about the charges against their clients.
When asked about those claims, the Bahraini government said in a statement that all of the defendants had been “afforded their full legal rights and safeguards, including the right of defense,” and that complaints of mistreatment would be referred for investigation.
“This case was about criminal conduct, not faith or belief,” the government added.
The Bahraini authorities had accused the defendants of forming a “terrorist group” linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps of Iran. According to a statement from the Bahraini public prosecution department, published by the state news agency, the defendants had worked to undermine the Bahraini government, and the group’s leaders had received “assignments and instructions” from Iranian officials.
“They had also sought to change the system of government by force and unlawful means through incitement to commit terrorist acts, acts of rioting and sabotage,” the statement added.

articles.title_zh: Warhammer Survivors roadmap reveals a bunch of free updates are on the way
articles.content_orig:
Vampire Survivors and its plethora of clones are always more fun in hour ten than hour one. The passive nature of the auto-attack gameplay means this style of experience lives or dies by how fun and visually over-the-top the action can get once you upgrade your character, gain access to more weapons, and manage to survive long enough to level up or evolve your weapons.
I did eventually hit that point of satisfaction with Warhammer Survivors , which was developed by Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 studio Auroch Digital with help from Vampire Survivors creator Poncle. When I got to the point where I could rip and tear through enemies with a Typhoon Crossbow as followers with upgraded weapons of their own fired at enemies around it, the game offered spectacle worthy of the Warhammer and Survivors names. But getting there doesn’t feel quite as good as its inspiration.
Warhammer Survivors doesn’t contain any sort of important lore to speak of; it’s more of a hodgepodge of various recognizable Warhammer characters (like Boltgun’s Malum Caedo) fighting against waves of unrelenting creatures from both eras of the franchise. Warhammer Survivors is essentially two games in one, with one half based on the sci-fi Warhammer 40,000 and the other on the more fantasy-like Warhammer: Age of Sigmar .
Each half of Warhammer Survivors has unique characters, weapons, enhancements, and objectives to unlock, but the core gameplay loop of each is the same. As a player, all you have to do is walk around levels as your character automatically attacks. Enemies drop experience when they die most of the time, and you collect that to level up and upgrade all of the weapons that you have equipped. Considering Poncle was directly involved with this game, it’s not surprising that Warhammer Survivors does not do much to hide its inspiration or reinvent the formula.
The most unique gimmick here is a follower feature, which solves for the fact that Warhammer Survivors’ characters are connected to factions that only let them use specific weapons. Rather than one character wielding every weapon and upgrading at once, sometimes you can save or summon another character that uses a different weapon to fight alongside you. This feels fitting for the large-scale battles Warhammer is known for. Yet in practice, all it really does is add an additional layer to a choice you were already going to make regardless.
It shouldn’t be too surprising that what you’re getting with this game is Vampire Survivors with a Warhammer coat of paint, even if it does go a bit deeper than Vampire Survivors’ typical crossover DLC . Vampire Survivors is a great game, and Warhammer Survivors is a good one too. That said, I won’t herald Warhammer Survivors as some amazing replacement for that indie classic, because there are some things it doesn’t do quite as well as the original.
Survivors games are all about snowballing power, building up to a chaotic storm of attacks. In Vampire Survivors , almost every weapon has auto aim and will hit something in range when used. But that’s not the case for certain early-game weapons in Warhammer Survivors that shoot the direction the player is facing, like the Boltgun. Those simply don’t mesh well with the auto-attacking gameplay.
The lack of auto-aim on these weapons meant that, as I moved to avoid enemies, I would shoot away from the horde, toward nothing. Eventually, I was able to unlock better weapons that would actually hit the enemies approaching me, but the fact that the earliest weapons are some of the worst means it takes a bit too long to find the fun.
By hour 10 with Vampire Survivors , I had found the characters and weapons I enjoyed using the most. They tended to be the ones that would allow me to exponentially increase in power most smoothly and actually felt like I could survive 20+ minutes and 40+ levels into a single run. From that point onwards, Warhammer Survivors is as good as Vampire Survivors or any other game of its ilk. It’s just not quite as instantly captivating and rewarding.
Diehard Warhammer fans who haven’t played Vampire Survivors or any of the games it inspired will have a fantastic time with this, but there’s not much reason to abandon the original Vampire Survivors for this official clone. Warhammer Survivors certainly won’t usurp its direct inspiration as my go-to game of this style because it forgets to emulate some of what made Vampire Survivors near-perfect. Still, it confidently delivers exactly what the title promises.
